cells.tense: You are with the work at the point where it holds without you.
cells.ask: Point to the one piece you have made that would keep working if you stepped away. Tell someone why you built it that way.
cells.core:
You know the difference between work that is finished and work you have simply stopped touching, and you are standing on the first kind. What you have made holds its shape without you in the room. You chose the shape, you kept at it past the interesting part, and now it carries other people whether or not you are watching. That is rarer than it sounds.

What got it here is also what is being asked for next: keep holding this without gripping it. A thing that stands on its own can be leaned on too hard by the one who built it, and you are close enough to do that. So let the practice set the pace for a while. What you made is speaking for itself now. Your job this year is to let it, and to notice what it is teaching the people who use it.
cells.sheetLine: What you built now stands without you holding it.
cells.verb: carrying a built thing through to where it stands on its own
cells.place: the table where a practice gets handed to the next person

cells.tense: You are already living in a finished version of this that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are about to finish and leave it deliberately imperfect this week. Let someone use it before it is ready.
cells.core:
You can see the finished version so clearly that the unfinished one in front of you keeps losing. Every draft gets measured against a completion that has not arrived, and the gap reads as failure rather than as the middle. So you push harder, extend the plan, add one more pass — and the thing that was nearly there gets postponed again.

The pressure is not ambition exactly. It is that you cannot yet feel the thing as done unless it is flawless, and flawless keeps moving. What would help is not more force. It is letting something real and imperfect out where people can use it and tell you what it is. You do not have to feel finished to hand it over. Hand it over and the feeling follows.
cells.sheetLine: You postpone the finished thing by insisting it be flawless.

cells.tense: You stopped short of the end of something and the stopping is still where you live.
cells.ask: Name the one thing you left at eighty percent and do its last step today, in whatever rough form is available.
cells.core:
There is an unfinished thing near you and you have been standing at a distance from it, describing yourself as someone who cannot see things through. That description has quietly become the plan. What is actually true is narrower: one thing rests, and you have been generalizing from it ever since.

You know how to keep going. You have done it plenty of times. What has gone quiet is the way you look at what is in front of you — you have stopped seeing it plainly, so everything reads as half-built at best. Pick up the nearest unfinished thing and look at it directly. Not the whole backlog. One thing, seen as it is, and finished in whatever form it can honestly take.
cells.sheetLine: You are not someone who quits. One thing is unfinished.

cells.tense: You are already the one people copy from, and you keep calling it circumstance.
cells.ask: Tell one person the next thing you intend to build, out loud, before you have started it.
cells.core:
People around you are already carrying things you made. A way of saying it, a way of running the meeting, a habit they picked up watching you — it is out there and it has your fingerprints on it, whether or not you say so. The building is done. Your word on it is not.

What makes this hard is that you have been treating your own influence as something that happens to you rather than something you set going. So the effort keeps going into the next build while the last one runs unnamed in other people's hands. Say plainly that you made the thing you made. Not to be credited. To know what you are steering. A person who names their own direction can choose the next one. A person who does not just keeps finding themselves in rooms they somehow ended up in.
cells.sheetLine: You built the thing people are copying. Say so.
cells.verb: carrying a built thing through to where it stands on its own

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the structure you built is standing complete and wanted — the record shows completion, not that anyone thanked you for it or that it should keep standing, and a reader could rightly say the thing is not finished and not theirs. The reader's likely objection: 'I have not finished anything; I am still in the middle of building it.' The ask survives being wrong because noticing what outlasts you and saying out loud why it was built does not depend on any cycle having closed — it works in the middle too. The sentence that serves me more than the person: anything that congratulates them for patience or frames the waiting as noble; cut it.
